title: The ancient yoga and why Krishna comes again

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचइमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् । विवस्वान् मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥
verses.tr: The Lord says: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvan. Vivasvan taught it to Manu, and Manu taught it to Ikshvaku.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After teaching the path of action, Krishna now turns to an ancient inheritance. Listen to the chain of teachers he names.

body.text: The Lord says: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvan. Vivasvan taught it to Manu, and Manu taught it to Ikshvaku. Notice the word avyayam, imperishable. Krishna calls this yoga imperishable because it has survived across ages, even though it was lost and is now being restored to Arjuna. Krishna continues by explaining that this imperishable teaching was passed down through royal sages before being lost to time.

verses.sa: एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः । स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥
verses.tr: O scorcher of foes, this yoga was known by the royal sages through an unbroken lineage. In the course of great time, this yoga was lost in this world.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Carry on from the line of kings, and listen to the word Krishna uses to call Arjuna.

body.text: O scorcher of foes, this yoga was known by the royal sages through an unbroken lineage. In the course of great time, this yoga was lost in this world. Arjuna is called Parantapa, scorcher of foes, and with that single name Krishna reminds him of his warrior nature as he speaks of a yoga once passed down by royal sages. Krishna says that because Arjuna is his friend and devotee, this ancient yoga is now being taught to him today.

verses.sa: स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः । भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥
verses.tr: Because you are my devotee and my friend, I have taught you today this ancient yoga. It is a supreme secret.
verses.angle: Friendship and devotion as the gateway
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just claimed that this teaching is ancient. Now he tells Arjuna exactly why he is hearing it. Listen to the reason.

body.text: Because you are my devotee and my friend, I have taught you today this ancient yoga. It is a supreme secret. Krishna shares this supreme secret only with Arjuna because they share the bond of a devotee and a close friend. That relationship makes the hidden knowledge possible. Arjuna now questions how an ancient teaching can come from a friend born recently.

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचअपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः । कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: Your birth is recent, while the birth of the Sun is ancient. How am I to understand that you taught this yoga at the beginning of creation?
verses.angle: The gap between Krishna's recent birth and the Sun's ancient birth
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has heard Krishna call this yoga ancient and secret. Now Arjuna points to the gap between Krishna's youth and the Sun's age.

body.text: Arjuna says: Your birth is recent, while the birth of the Sun is ancient. How am I to understand that you taught this yoga at the beginning of creation? Arjuna hears that the yoga was taught at the beginning of creation, yet he sees Krishna standing before him as a living charioteer, while the Sun is ancient. He asks how this can be. Krishna answers that many births have passed for both of them, and only he remembers them all.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचबहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन । तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥
verses.tr: Krishna says: Many births of yours and mine have passed, Arjuna. I know them all, but you do not, enemy-burner.
verses.angle: वेत्थ: what you know and do not know
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna opens a vast frame. He says they have both crossed many births. Listen for the sharp difference between what he knows and what you know.

body.text: Krishna says: Many births of yours and mine have passed, Arjuna. I know them all, but you do not, enemy-burner. Krishna and Arjuna have both lived many births; Krishna remembers them all, Arjuna does not. Krishna now explains how you can know this truth, even though you do not remember your own past.

verses.sa: अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् । प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया ॥
verses.tr: Though unborn and imperishable, and though I am the lord of all beings, I manifest myself by controlling my own nature through my own power of appearance.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has asked how Krishna could have taught the sun at the dawn of time. The answer is that ordinary birth does not bind this speaker at all. Listen to how he describes his own power.

body.text: Though unborn and imperishable, and though I am the lord of all beings, I manifest myself by controlling my own nature through my own power of appearance. Unborn and imperishable, Krishna still appears, taking form through his own power over nature. He explains that he appears whenever dharma declines and adharma rises.

verses.sa: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत । अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥
verses.tr: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and a rise of adharma, I manifest myself.
verses.angle: Whenever: a recurring crisis in history
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna he is unborn and knows all births. Now he explains exactly when he enters the world.

body.text: Whenever there is a decline of dharma and a rise of adharma, I manifest myself. Whenever dharma declines and adharma rises, Krishna says, he manifests himself. He then names the precise purpose of this repeated appearance: to protect the good, destroy the wicked, and establish dharma.

verses.sa: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ॥
verses.tr: For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of wrongdoers, and for the establishment of dharma, I appear age after age.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just said he appears when dharma declines. Now he tells Arjuna the exact purpose behind that appearing. Listen for the three tasks that drive his descent.

body.text: For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of wrongdoers, and for the establishment of dharma, I appear age after age. Krishna comes age after age to protect the good, destroy wrongdoers and re-establish dharma. Krishna then tells Arjuna that understanding this cycle of appearing and acting in the world is the key to liberation.

verses.sa: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः । त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, my birth and action are divine. One who truly understands this does not take birth again after leaving the body, but comes to me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna speaks of his own birth and action as something beyond the ordinary. Listen to how he links this knowledge to a person's fate.

body.text: Arjuna, my birth and action are divine. One who truly understands this does not take birth again after leaving the body, but comes to me. The word divyam means divine. Krishna is saying that his birth and his actions are not bound by the laws of nature, and knowing this truth is what frees a person. Many purified beings have already reached this state by taking refuge in him. Listen to how they did it.

verses.sa: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः । बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥
verses.tr: Many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, free from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me and taking refuge in Me, have attained My being.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from his divine birth to the inner state of those who reach him. Listen for the austerity that purifies the mind.

body.text: Many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, free from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me and taking refuge in Me, have attained My being. Listen for jnanatapasa, the austerity of knowledge. It is not a physical penance but the steady discipline of wisdom that burns away impurity and leads to the divine. Krishna now states that he responds directly to the way people approach him, so every path leads back to him.

verses.sa: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् । मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
verses.tr: As people approach Me, so I respond to them. All people follow My path in every way, O Arjuna.
verses.angle: Bhajami: the divine meets each approach
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described how purified seekers take refuge in him. Now he explains how he responds to anyone who approaches, and how every person is already following his path.

body.text: As people approach Me, so I respond to them. All people follow My path in every way, O Arjuna. Listen to the verb bhajami, meaning I favor or respond to. It shows that the divine is not a distant judge but an active presence that meets every seeker according to their own approach. Krishna now explains why people who want quick results worship radiant beings instead of him.

verses.sa: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः । क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥
verses.tr: People who want quick success worship radiant beings, because results from action come quickly in the human world.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries on from his teaching that all paths lead to Him, and now He shows why people still look elsewhere for quick fixes.

body.text: People who want quick success worship radiant beings, because results from action come quickly in the human world. The word kanksantah, desiring, reveals the restless pull of the mind. People do not worship the devas because they are wise; they do so because they want fast results, and in the human world action can indeed produce quick fruit. Krishna now turns to the very origin of these divisions and the social orders that bind them together.

verses.sa: चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः । तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥
verses.tr: The four social orders were created by Me according to qualities and actions. Though I am their maker, know Me as the unchanging non-doer.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna answers why the world is divided into roles by revealing that even the maker of those roles remains untouched by them. Listen for that paradox.

body.text: The four social orders were created by Me according to qualities and actions. Though I am their maker, know Me as the unchanging non-doer. Here is the core paradox: Krishna says he is the maker of the four orders, yet he asks Arjuna to know him as the changeless non-doer. The creator of the system is not trapped inside it. Krishna then adds that actions do not stain him, because he has no craving for their fruits. One who knows this is not bound.

verses.sa: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा । इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥
verses.tr: Actions do not stain me, and I do not crave their fruits. One who knows me this way is not bound by actions.
verses.angle: karma and phala, action and fruit
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna explains why he remains untouched by action. Listen to how he separates the work from the hunger for results.

body.text: Actions do not stain me, and I do not crave their fruits. One who knows me this way is not bound by actions. Actions do not stain Krishna because he has no craving for their fruit, and knowing this frees you. He shows that even ancient seekers of freedom acted this way, so you must do your duty.
